general: Focus on the weakest S first; it moves the overall score fastest.
Set a 30-day target per zone and re-audit weekly.
Assign a named owner for each zone.
Post scores and before/after photos on the zone board.

sort: Run a red-tag campaign and dispose of tagged items within 7 days.
Mark approved locations on the floor with the operators.
Do a 15-minute weekly sweep per zone.
Assign one owner per zone for red-tag follow-up.
order: Use shadow boards and labelled locations for tools.
Remove items that block access during a layout walk.
shine: Create a cleaning roster with a named owner per zone.
Add a cleaning checklist at shift start and sign-off at shift end.
Fix the source of dust or leaks instead of cleaning repeatedly.
standardize: Publish a one-page visual standard per zone.
Align the audit checklist with the visual standard.
Use colour coding for storage and inspection points.
Train new staff on the zone standard before they start.
sustain: Run weekly audits with rotating auditors.
Display results and actions on the zone board.
Convert repeat findings into cards with owners and dates.
Add a short 5S review to the daily meeting.

general: Stratify failures by machine, shift and test before acting.
Fix the highest-volume recurring failure first.
Add a pre-start check for the tests that fail most.
Record the corrective action against the failed test.

actions: Verify calibration status and due dates.

Check the lab press calibration.

Retain a repeat sample for confirmation.

general: Compare planned vs actual at line and shift level before acting.
Check changeover and start-up losses first.
Separate availability losses from rate and quality losses.
Fix the largest loss category before adding capacity.

actions: Review shift start-up and changeover time against standard.
Check feed rate and raw-material availability.
Remove the top downtime cause for the line.
Set a daily recovery target with the shift team.
Stratify rejects by product, line and shift.
Verify process parameters against the recipe.
Check incoming material lots.
Add an in-process check at the highest-loss point.
Split cost variance into energy, material and maintenance.
Check specific energy consumption per tonne.
Review overtime and contractor spend.
Set a monthly cost-per-tonne target by plant.

general: Rank downtime by total hours, not by number of events.
Investigate the top three machines first.
Add preventive tasks for repeating causes.
Track mean time to repair for each major machine.

actions: Add vibration and temperature checks to the PM route.
Check alignment and belt tension after every intervention.
Hold critical spares for the top recurring items.
Review the PM frequency against failure history.
Thermographically scan panels and connections.
Clean and torque panel connections during stops.
Check motor load and protection settings.
Log every trip with the operating condition.
Inspect chute liners and transfer points.
Add a blockage-prevention check to the shift routine.
Review material moisture and feed consistency.
Train operators on the correct restart procedure.
